proposal.scope: Simulates all 18 family members (3 put modes x 3 channel modes x 2 trigger states) and keeps those consistent with calibration receipts; answers only when all consistent members agree.
proposal.lesson: The channel is not net committed effects: changes() reflects the last statement's direct row changes, total_changes accumulates per connection, and an AFTER INSERT trigger adds one to total_changes but not to changes(). REPLACE counts a row change even when the value is unchanged, while IGNORE and DO UPDATE do not. Filtering the family by receipts and intersecting predictions preserves uncertainty for underdetermined goals.

def investigate(context, acquire):
    return {"value": None, "unresolved": True}

proposal.scope: Predicts channel, committed_count, or committed_sum for a fresh action sequence by simulating all 18 family members (put mode x channel x trigger) and keeping those consistent with calibration receipts; resolves only when all consistent candidates agree.
proposal.lesson: The calibration receipts show put on existing key yields channel 2 with committed_sum 2, indicating REPLACE or UPSERT (not IGNORE). The rollback receipt shows channel 2 with committed_sum 1, meaning the first put (value 1) contributed 1 to channel and the rolled-back put contributed 1, consistent with total_changes or changes() where the second put still counted. The other-connection receipt shows channel 2, so channel includes other connection's changes (total_both) or the second put on other connection counted. The begin/put/put/commit receipt shows channel 2 with committed_sum 47, meaning two puts inside transaction each counted 1, and final value 47 (REPLACE or UPSERT). These narrow candidates; the simulator generalizes to new sequences.
